newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia hikes Nov diesel purchases to 4 mln bbls.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia hikes Nov diesel purchases to 4 mln bbls.

text.p: Indonesia has doubled its diesel purchases for November delivery to at least four million barrels due to a refinery shutdown and a slight delay in restarting one of them from maintenance, industry sources said on Tuesday.

Traders said Indonesia, which normally imports between two and 2.5 million barrels a month, was forced to hike its purchases in part due to delays restarting a crude distillation unit (CDU) at the Cilacap refinery.

Pertamina restarted a 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude unit at Cilacap about one-week later than scheduled on October 7. But operations were not at full capacity due to startup problems at a 55,000-bpd visbreaker.
The visbreaker resumed operations on October 13. The Cilacap refinery complex, which is located in Central Java, has another CDU with a 100,000-bpd capacity.

On top of this, the 125,000-bpd Balongan refinery is currently down for a 40-day maintenance since October 1. The refinery's main secondary unit, a 83,000-bpd long residue catalytic cracker, will be down for about 60 days.
Traders said Indonesia had already bought six to seven 80,000-tonne diesel cargoes from several players for arrival in November, including one term cargo from a MidEast refiner.
Industry sources said the cargoes were sold at between 40 and 50 cents per barrel premiums to Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
Some traders said that Indonesia is still seeking more cargoes for arrival in November but this was not confirmed.

As a result of these purchases, diesel prices in Singapore have remained firm over the past few weeks despite declines in values in the west. Prices were also boosted on Monday following India's decision to buy 520,000-tonnes of diesel for December delivery.
The market had initially expected India to buy only around 300,000-tonnes due to port congestions.
Two 150,000-barrel cargoes of diesel traded on Monday at $30.40 and $30.50 per barrel on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis, up from Thursday's traded level of $29.70 per barrel.

Similarly gas oil swaps have also firmed over the past few days with November paper traded on Monday at a high of $30.70, up from Friday's close of $30.25/30.35. November swaps was last quoted at $30.60-30.60, brokers said.
